title: T16b: read Outlook calendar and unread mail through Microsoft Graph
head: codex/t16b-outlook-read
body:
## What

Part of T16b (make daily-summary real on Braden's Mac; decisions #48-#51).

New `gates.graph_read`: async `calendar_today` (connector `outlook-calendar`, today's events, drops cancelled and declined, all-day marked, `truncated` if more pages) and `unread_mail` (connector `outlook`: inbox `unreadItemCount` plus up to 10 newest unread headers: subject, sender, received time; bodies and `bodyPreview` are never requested or kept).

Subjects and titles are sanitized (control characters stripped, 200-char cap) and treated as data.

Audit lines use new actions `read_calendar` / `read_mail` and hold no content (no subjects, senders, tokens, URLs).

Async token refresh (`oauth_http`), one retry on 401, HTTPS Graph host only, no redirects, 15 s timeout, 64 KiB cap.

`catalog/outlook/connector.yaml` notes subjects/senders are `internal`, bodies stay `restricted`.

`docs/registrations.md` corrected: Microsoft admin consent granted 2026-09-22.

Version 0.3.0 (`pyproject.toml`, `gates.__version__`, `uv.lock`).

New `docs/graph-read.md`, `tests/test_graph_read.py` (all via `httpx.MockTransport`).

## Not yet proven

Graph query syntax and field names are written from API knowledge; workers had no network.

Braden's live Mac run is the real proof.

After merge, the coordinator builds the 0.3.0 wheel from the merge commit and vendors it into `agent-core` with its SHA256.

## Checks (rerun by coordinator)

`pytest -q` → 214 passed

`ruff check .` → All checks passed

`ruff format --check` on changed files → formatted (4 older files in `scripts/` and `tests/test_registration.py` were already unformatted on main and are untouched)

`mypy --strict src` → no issues in 13 files (native and `--platform win32`)

`git diff --check` → clean
